ground_truth_witness:
HEADLINE WITNESS (n = 6, connected, BFS-consistent layering, positive expansion; independently re-verified by hand-written code at the end of the script).

Graph G: V = {0,1,2,3,4,5}, E = {01, 04, 12, 13, 24, 25, 35}.
Layers: W_1 = {0,1}, W_2 = {2,3,4}, W_3 = {5}. These are EXACTLY the BFS layers from W_1 (W_k = vertices at distance k-1 from W_1), so every edge is inside a layer or between consecutive layers, as in the proof's setting.
Cascade: R_1 = {0} ⊆ W_1, R_2 = N(R_1) ∩ W_2 = {1,4} ∩ {2,3,4} = {4}, R_3 = N(R_2) ∩ W_3 = {0,2} ∩ {5} = ∅. So m = 3, and "by construction R_{m-1} = R_2 = {4} has no edges to W_m = W_3" holds — the exact hypothesis the quoted sentence invokes. (Under the alternative reading R_{m-1} := {v ∈ W_{m-1} : v has no edge into W_m}, the same set {4} results, so the witness is robust to which reading of R_{m-1} the source intends.)
Case 2 hypothesis: |R_2| = 1 < n/2 = 3. Padding inside W_{m-1} is possible since |W_2| = 3 ≥ n/2 = 3.
Padded set: S = R_2 ∪ {2,3} = {2,3,4}, R_2 ⊆ S ⊆ W_2, |S| = 3 = n/2. This is the ONLY admissible padded set here, so the failure is universal, not an artifact of an unlucky "arbitrary" choice.
Recomputed quantities:
  N(S) = {0,1,5}.  N(S) ∩ W_m = {5}.
  Proof claims |N(S) ∩ W_m| = 0 (i.e. N(S) ⊆ V \ W_m); here |N(S) ∩ W_m| = 1 > 0.
  Exact expansion of G (Fractions): min_{0<|T|≤n/2} |N(T)|/n = 1/3 and min |N(T)|/|T| = 2/3, so G is connected and satisfies the ambient expansion hypothesis |N(T)| ≥ αn for all |T| ≤ n/2 with α = 1/3.
  The proof's next step |N(S)| ≤ αn then reads |N(S)| ≤ 2, whereas |N(S)| = 3 > 2 — the intended contradiction with the expansion hypothesis is not obtained.

Smallest witness found (n = 4): path 0-2-1-3 with W_1={0}, W_2={1,2}, W_3={3}, R_1={0}, R_2={2}, R_3=∅; the unique padded set S = {1,2} has N(S) ∩ W_3 = {3} ≠ ∅.

Witness counts in the searched space: 4 (n=4), 8032 (n=6), 22400 (n=8) counterexample instances; script runtime 122.7 s wall with <mount-root><machine-root>/anonymous-user/partB_venv/bin/python.
ground_truth_flaw: In the second case of its case split (|R_{m-1}| < n/2), the proof pads R_{m-1} with arbitrary extra vertices of W_{m-1} to form S with |S| = n/2, and then asserts that S still has "no neighbor in W_m" with the justification "since S ⊇ R_{m-1}". This inference is unsound: only R_{m-1} is known to have no neighbors in W_m; the padding vertices of W_{m-1} \ R_{m-1} are merely unreachable from W_1, which places no restriction on their adjacency to W_m. Hence the deduction N(S) ⊆ V \ W_m and |N(S)| ≤ αn does not follow, and the contradiction with the expansion hypothesis is not established in this case.
